the growth trajectory of M. sexta is a truncated Gompetz curve and that this trajectory depends on nutrition and temperature.

the size increment increases with instar number and that the size increment is independent of temperature, that the critical weight for molting increases with instar and that the critical weight decreases with temperature.
the size increment increases from instar to the next instar and that the mass-specific growth decreases throughout the larval growth phase.

the growth of Manduca larvae is a complex, dynamic process that can be described by a set of quantitative relationships.

Manduca has evolved a mechanism that allows it to maintain a constant size at metamorphosis despite a progressive increase in body mass during larval life and despite the fact that growth rate declines throughout larval life.
the size and age at which Manduca stops growing are controlled by the rate at which growth slows, which in turn is controlled by temperature and nutrition.
